rules: Import `ruststream_pulsar::prelude::*` at a mount site and name the policy `Publish` there; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` and bounds a slot with a capability such as `Out<impl Publisher>` (Components > Broker > Prelude).

Describe a subscription with `PulsarSubscription::new(topic, name)` for one topic, `::topics([..], name)` for a fixed list or `::pattern(regex, name)` for every topic whose full name matches (Components > Subscriptions).
Mount a handler written without the macros as `subscriber(PulsarSubscription::new(..), Body)`, the descriptor passed as the source as it is (Components > Subscriptions > PulsarSubscription).

Use bare `#[subscriber("orders")]` with `PulsarBroker::default_subscription(name)` for a `Shared` subscription with default settings; name a `PulsarSubscription` for any other setting (Components > Subscriptions).

Pick `SubscriptionType::KeyShared` to keep each key's order across consumers, `Shared` for any consumer, and `Exclusive` or `Failover` for one reader, bounding `OperationRetries` to fail fast (Components > Subscriptions > SubscriptionType).

Settle through the handler's outcome: `ack()` and `drop()` acknowledge, `retry()` negatively acknowledges, and `ack_timeout` on the descriptor redelivers an unsettled message (Components > Settlement).

Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(topic)` after `include` on a `Shared` or `KeyShared` subscription; the Pulsar client counts the deliveries and moves the spent message (Guides > Retries and dead letters).
Take a batch with a slice handler and `.batch(n)` at the mount site, and set `batch_wait` on the descriptor to close a partial one (Components > Subscriptions > Batches).
Replay the retained log with `start_at(PulsarPosition::earliest())` on every startup, and move a running subscription from its handler through `Ctx<SeekHandle>` (Guides > Replay and seeking).
Publish and reply through `Publish` at the mount site (`.out_reply(Publish)`, `.out(Marker, Publish).build()`); a request-reply exchange is a publish to another topic (Components > Publishing).

Key one publish with the `partition_key` step on a slot bounded `Out<impl Publisher<Options = PulsarPublishOptions>, Marker>`, or write the `partition-key` header (Components > Publishing > partition_key).
Build a topic name from code with `PulsarTopic::persistent` or `non_persistent`, and parse one read at run time with `PulsarTopic::parse` (Components > Subscriptions > PulsarTopic).

Test the production app: hand the app `main` runs to `TestApp::start` with the `testing` feature, address the broker as `tb.broker::<PulsarBroker>()`, and run the same body on `TestApp::start_live` (Components > Testing).

Give `PulsarBroker::new` one service URL, `pulsar://` or `pulsar+ssl://`, of a DNS name, load balancer or proxy in front of the cluster, and attach a JWT with `token` (Guides > Connecting to a production cluster).
